column1: # Short forms of decision titles: id, decision number, short form.
# Written by hand beside the generated titles.tsv; cite-rewrite uses a short form in place of the
# heading when one exists. Each short form keeps the meaning of the heading, adds no claim, and holds
# no enhancement id or decision number. Rows cover every title over 110 characters and every title
# that holds an id. Keep this file sorted by id and number.

column3: `#ctx` collapses to `{ release, components }`; no `runtime` axis, no `module` mirror
`#Component.#release` is the per-component release injection slot, wired by `#Module`
Cross-catalog primitive references are a documented supported pattern; no kernel-level manifest
`MissingFQN` is one structured diagnostic per `(release, component, FQN)` triple
`#Blueprint` follows the same SemVer and stamping trail as `#Resource`, `#Trait` and `#ComponentTransformer`
This entry lands on top of the core split's Part B; library and modules slices wait for `remove-api-binding-dispatch`
Catalog repackage is a hard switch; no graceful coexistence with the legacy `@v1` shape
Library kernel pulls the core schema from the OCI registry; the `//go:embed` of `apis/core/` is deleted
The catalog family is in scope; each catalog CUE module bumps `@v0 → @v1` on a forward-alpha line
The invariant is enforced at **acquire**, in `library`; publish-side derivation is not sufficient
Publish never honours `cue.mod/local-module.cue`, and refuses while replacements exist
`#Catalog` has `metadata.version` removed, with the major carried in the path
The CLI's platform source is a precedence: flag, then cluster Platform CR, then local default
`Platform` carries no owner marker; the operator always owns the singleton
The CLI imports `library` only; it does not import `opm-operator`
Both a local Platform and an in-cluster Platform CR are first-class; OPM never requires cluster-admin
After handoff the CLI may still edit the CR's spec; it writes only the CR and defers execution to the operator
Platform-source flag surface: a single `--platform <file>` override plus automatic precedence
Solo-cluster `Platform` write-if-absent uses a plain `Create` that tolerates `AlreadyExists`
Status-subresource RBAC: opt-in `--rbac` emission and a pre-flight access check
CRD and operator version skew: a CLI-at-least-cluster invariant, enforced by a gate only
Install commands are verb-first (`opm install operator`, `opm install crds`, `opm uninstall operator`)
`instance list --all-namespaces` is a native cluster-wide CR list; a clear error on insufficient RBAC
The render-digest parity experiment is deferred into the kernel-adoption slice
Revert the shared `library/opm/inventory` package; the CLI and operator keep independent local inventory implementations
Noun-first `opm operator` command group (`opm operator install`, `opm operator uninstall`)
Slice B2 ships install and uninstall only; the missing-CRD apply gate moves to C1
`opm operator uninstall` preserves the namespace and refuses while cleanup finalizers are armed
One embedded artifact, `dist/install.yaml`, with CRDs as a filtered subset and a pinned version
The CLI's CUE bump retargets to v0.17.1 and relocates from C2 to C1
`cue.mod/local-module.cue` is the sanctioned local-module workflow; the CR never represents a local path
The provenance annotation is kept and promoted to a fail-closed handoff pre-gate
`~/.opm` becomes two import-free data files; the local default platform is the sibling `~/.opm/platform.cue`
Handoff success is "inventory-stable reconcile", not byte-no-op
An unresolved primitive demand is an error; a trait's optionality is stated by its catalog
A contract declares where its fulfilment comes from; a provider-fulfilled contract admits exactly one provider
The first-party catalogs consolidate into one, `catalog_opm`, on the v2 line
Modules carry an identity subpackage and a version; `version set` and `--version` behave identically
The authored version is the trigger; an already-published version is always a refusal
The Kubernetes runtime surface homes in the library's Kubernetes tier
The Kubernetes runtime decisions live in a fenced tier, `opm/k8s`, inside the library module
Ordering is kind-class order in the Kubernetes tier; cross-module order belongs to a future Bundle
The apply guard runs on every apply, refusing foreign objects outside the inventory and objects adopted by another instance
SOPS support lands at the file seams, decrypt on input and encrypt on export
The rewrite is omission at build assembly, measured viable on the real kernel path
A secret source is a catalog-defined resource; the platform installs any number side by side
No transformer-predicate stability rule in this entry; the widening gate is deferred
A build-incompatible registration is refused at acceptance, by comparing committed resolutions
The claim names a published catalog artifact, and only that
Every field of the claim is derived or stamped; the only authored fact is the catalog dependency version
The platform package regenerates edge-triggered and level-computed, keyed by generation plus the active-claim set
`#Module` gains an optional field carrying the author-intended init template
`opm instance init` mirrors `opm module init` and takes a major-free module path
The generated module file pins the module exactly and carries core at the module's major
Catalog version skew between a module and its platform is detected by the kernel
Sibling access through `#moduleInstance` stays reachable and is discouraged by contract
The render module's `cue.mod` is derived by promotion, never computed
Skew policy defaults to warn-and-render; the comparison reads the two committed resolutions
The sweep extends to `catalogs/k8s`, with that catalog's exact-name carve-outs enumerated
Three name types: the label stays the safety floor and the subdomain becomes the override ceiling
Dot-hostile primitives declare a `#nameConstraint`; the component asserts the resolved name against their conjunction
A primitive computes its `#nameConstraint` from its own state
A computed `#nameConstraint` must resolve on every attachment path
The block lives at `custom."opmodel.dev@v0"` in `cue.mod/module.cue`
`#ModuleTransformer` is `#ComponentTransformer` transposed; it never sees rendered output
Aspects participate in the platform's matching and contract inventory
This entry ships the extension point and no vocabulary
A platform admits catalog lineages through a pure-data `#Platform` of `#CatalogAdmission` entries
The shipped platform value moves to `#ResolvedPlatform`, generated per resolution from the authored `#Platform` and the pins
Provider catalogs use the same entry shape; the registration's derived version is the pick when no consumer pins the path
An admission entry for a provider catalog is optional and, when present, its range overrides the author's window
The shared-path requirement check runs per render against the consumer's pins
A platform-owned, cluster-scoped definition binds the module
The consumer-facing schema is the module's `#config`, enforced at the API server
The platform authors the binding; the module never emits the definition
